chunks: From him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from one of the two of them عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him: “Is a single adhan sufficient?” He said: “If you pray in congregation, nothing suffices except an adhan and an iqamah. But if you are alone and hastening to something that you fear may escape you, an iqamah suffices for you, except in the fajr and maghrib prayers, for it is appropriate that you give the adhan in them both and perform the iqamah, because shortening is not done in them as it is done in the rest of the prayers.”

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: the call announcing the immediate commencement of salat

ai.seo_question: When is iqamah alone sufficient, and when are both adhan and iqamah required in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the sufficiency of adhan and iqamah in salat. In congregational prayer, both the adhan and iqamah are required, while for a person praying alone in haste, the iqamah alone may suffice except in fajr and maghrib, where both should be recited.
